Angular_Leaf_Spot.quote: Leaf symptoms first appear as gray to dark-brown irregular or angular spots with necrotic centers and yellow halos.
Large, circular, reddish-brown lesions with concentric rings (bullseye appearance) develop on affected pods.

Common_Bacterial_Blight_Of_Beans.quote: Small, water-soaked spots (Figure 1), usually more evident on the underside of the leaves become larger and develop into dry, brown spots with distinct, rather narrow, yellow halos.
Large, water-soaked areas (Figure 4). These areas are more or less circular and slightly sunken can become distinctly brick-red in color and more deeply pitted.
Early pod infection causes shriveled seeds, and the bacteria may cause yellow to orange discoloration under the seed coat of infected seeds.
